newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - Olivetti slides on share reduction plan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Olivetti slides on share reduction plan.

text.p: Shares in Italy's Olivetti sunk lower on Wednesday as investors took fright of a capital reduction announced late Tuesday along with group's results which will cut the number of Olivetti shares in issue.
The stock was suspended at the Milan bourse's 10 percent limit down level before bourse authorities extended the limit to 15 percent. The shares last traded down 8.22 percent at 509 lire at 1245 GMT.

The capital restructuring, if approved by a extraordinary general meeting, will reduce the nominal value of the shares to 640 lire from 1,000 lire and then through a reverse split, or regrouping, bring the nominal value back to 1,000 lire, thus reducing the number of shares in issue.

In effect, Olivetti shareholders will swop 1.56 of their old shares for one new Olivetti share, or close to a three-for-two exchange, and analysts are concerned that the new shares will not be worth much more than the old shares.
"It is difficult to imagine the shares bouncing back in the short-term and they look to continue under pressure," said Marco Nascimbeni at Merrill Lynch in Milan.
Analysts said there were few indications to suggest trading conditions were improving at Olivetti, although some suggested the picture was stabilising in the first quarter of 1997.
"An air of normality has returned, but there a few signs that the businesses are actually improving," said one London-based industry analyst.

Olivetti's capital reduction was to comply with Italian regulations which says that if a holding company has losses greater than a third of its total capital then it needs to call an EGM and to discuss a reduction of the group's capital.
Olivetti's holding company Olivetti SpA announced a net loss of 1.406 trillion lire ($827 million) in 1996 late Tuesday, and prompted the need for a capital reduction.
Analysts said that the move will do little to help the share price return to the 1,000 lire nominal value where the price needs to be to launch a successful rights issue.

Olivetti chief executive Roberto Colaninno has said in his rescue plan that after 1.2 trillion lire of asset sales are completed in 1996 and 1997, the group may need a rights issue at the end of 1997 to refinance the company.

The group's new telecom interests -- its Telemedia company and 35.5 percent stake in mobile phone consortium Omnitel -- are still unprofitable and need cash, while its mature businesses have run into trading difficulties.
The group tried to paint a better picture for 1997 saying it expects to approach break-even at the pretax level and before anticipated losses from Omnitel.

Olivetti said its first quarter of 1997 showed a pretax loss of 180 billion lire as sales slipped 10.4 percent to 1.38 trillion lire, but its net financial requirement rose sharply to 2.70 trillion lire from 2.20 trillion lire at end-1996.

The group, which has not recorded a profit since 1990, also reported net losses in 1996 of 915 billion lire, compared to 1.60 trillion lire of losses in 1995 as sales fell 14.6 percent to 8.30 trillion lire from 1995 levels.
